'''Josephine Elizabeth Burns Glasgow''' (July 22, 1887 – January 22, 1969) was an American mathematician whose Ph.D. thesis, "The abstract definitions of the [[group (mathematics)|groups]] of degree 8" was published in the ''[[American Journal of Mathematics]]''.<ref>{{cite journal | author=Josephine Burns | title=The abstract definitions of the groups of degree 8 | journal=American Journal of Mathematics | volume=37 | number=2 | pages=192–214 | date=Apr 1915 }}</ref><ref name=agnes /> She was the second woman to receive a PhD from the [[University of Illinois]].

== Life ==

Glasgow was born in [[Greenville, Illinois]]. She was the third of four children. Her parents were Ida Jane and James Clinton Burns. Her father was a professor of history at [[Western Illinois University]].<ref name="green">{{cite book| first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's|date=2009|publisher=American Mathematical Society|isbn=9780821843765|title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics |at=[https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&lpg=PA182 p. 182]}} Biography on p.207-208 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref> 

She married Robert D. Glasgow in 1916.<ref name="agnes">{{cite web|title=Josephine Elizabeth Burns Glasgow|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/burns.htm|website=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|publisher=Agnes Scott College|accessdate=13 March 2017}}</ref>

In 1928 Glasgow's husband took a post as state [[entomologist]] of [[New York State]] and the couple moved to [[Albany, New York|Albany]]. Josephine became active in the [[American Association of University Women]], rising through various roles to be the vice president of the national board of directors in 1952. In 1951 the Albany section named a fellowship in her honour.<ref name=green />

== Career ==

Glasgow received her A.B. degree in 1909 and her master's degree in mathematics in 1911.<ref name=agnes /> She received her PhD from the [[University of Illinois]] in 1913, being the second woman to do so at that university. Her doctoral supervisor was [[George Abram Miller]].<ref name=green />

She was an instructor at the University of Illinois.<ref name=green />
